work_order.understanding: Issue #20 is the safety slice of epic #14 and it is greenfield. I verified independently of the proposal and the critique: there is no src/policy/, no src/executor/, no src/strategy/guardian.js, no approvals/capabilities/action_records/kill_switches/trust_ledger store anywhere under src/ or in db.js's MIGRATIONS (which end at 004_knowledge_tables, src/data/db.js:173). The approvals page today (src/web/pages.js:741-800) is a static shell: it reads raw events of type 'approval.requested' (no fixture ever writes one, so it is always empty), renders the hardcoded AUTONOMY_POSTURE constant at :734-739, and its Approve/Reject buttons at :791-792 have no listener in client.js. Nothing gates a mutation because there is no module between an ActionIntent and a provider write. I also verified two things the critique surfaced and the proposal missed: the repo already ships the atomic single-winner primitive this work needs (repositories.idempotency.claim, an INSERT OR IGNORE returning true iff this call created the claim, src/data/repositories.js:148, with a release at :158 for a failed effect), and maturityFor/policyBand are already imported by src/api/routes.js:16/19 but used only inside GET /v1/metrics (:157-158) — so the band gate has an existing, correct source of truth sitting one function away. The binding decision from the brief (and the issue body) is Meta Ads first, Google Ads later, so every write targets the Meta adapter seam. The five split criteria IAC-1..IAC-5 are each carried by one acceptance entry below.
work_order.root_cause: There is no write path to gate. The repo has no module between an ActionIntent and a provider write, so the safety contract this issue is asked for — TR-2 credential isolation, TR-3 signed capabilities, TR-4 kill switches, TR-5 nonce idempotency plus reconciliation, TR-19 per-class trust, TR-24 fail-closed writes — has no code to hold it. The approvals page cannot be more than a static shell because no approval row, receipt, capability or trust row is stored anywhere, and the autonomy posture it displays is a hardcoded array read by nothing.
work_order.approach:
Build the write path as four new modules plus one composition point, on the repo's existing patterns (additive migration, tenant-bound repositories, one pure function per rule, node:test suites mirroring src/). v5's diagnosis was right and I kept it. This revision answers the one recorded rejection by taking the reviewer's option (a) — implementing the gate — and then repairs the five places where v5's own gate was not actually the single owner it claimed to be.

ONE MINTER, ONE CHOKE POINT. The recorded rejection demanded that the trust ledger gate a write end to end, and v5 answered that correctly in principle (gate at issuance, because a capability cannot exist without passing validateIntent) but then specified the approve route with its own parallel gate, so the human-approval path — the money-moving one — skipped the micro-limit, the band and the no-evidence refusal. CORRECTED: both issuance routes (POST /v1/capabilities and POST /v1/approvals/:id/approve) call kernel.validateIntent(intent, {nowIso, trust, approval, maturity}) and nothing else may mint a capability. issueCapability takes the {ok, intent} object validateIntent returns, so a route physically cannot sign an unvalidated intent, and a static import-boundary assertion pins the only two call sites. The two routes are symmetric: the same gate, differing only in whether an approval row is supplied.

THE POSTURE LADDER, and what each rung does. monotonic, so no route can launder a class into authority:
  - shadow (or a pinned class, or one with no evidence at all) -> AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED on BOTH issuance routes, even with a valid pending approval. Shadow means authority has not been granted yet; a human approval is not a way around it. This is the fail-closed reading of TR-19 and TR-24.
  - approval-required -> issues only when a non-terminal, unexpired approval row for the same tenant and action class is supplied. The approval row is the authority; the micro-limit still applies.
  - autonomous-under-micro-limits -> issues with NO approval row. POST /v1/capabilities is that route, and it is what makes IAC-4 observable end to end.

THE FAILURE FIXTURE MUST BE APPROVABLE (corrects v5's own contradiction). v5 seeded its failure-path fixture as apr_seed_launch_1 (campaign-launch) while giving campaign-launch no ledger row, so the gate refused it outright and the provider-failure path AC-5 and the QA script depend on was unreachable through the gate it had just built. CORRECTED: the seed now carries FOUR ledger rows — campaign-status autonomous (6/6/0/0), budget-change approval-required, campaign-launch approval-required, new-geography pinned shadow — and creative-refresh alone carries no row, so the fail-closed no-evidence case is still demonstrated from real data on a real roster class rather than on the write-failure fixture. Both pending fixtures are then genuinely approvable, which is what the 'either ordering consumes exactly one item' arithmetic needs.

THE BAND IS WIRED, NOT ASSUMED. v5 listed maturity as an argument validateIntent takes and no route computes it, so in production the comparison was against undefined and failed open. CORRECTED: both issuance routes compute maturity with the maturityFor/policyBand pair the repo already uses in GET /v1/metrics (src/api/routes.js:16/19, :157-158) and pass it; and validateIntent treats a missing or non-numeric maturity as MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED, because a check that cannot read its input must not pass. The band remains the autonomy gate only — a human approval is the alternative authority for a class that has not earned autonomy (TR-7 read with TR-19) — and both directions are pinned by a test.

IDEMPOTENCY IS ATOMIC AND KEYED ON THE LOGICAL ACTION. v5's executor did getByNonce then write, which is check-then-act, and the approve route minted a fresh random nonce on every call, so a second tab or a retried POST of the same approval row produced two distinct nonces and wrote twice. CORRECTED in two parts. (1) The executor's dedupe uses the primitive the repo already ships: repositories.idempotency.claim(tenantId, nonce, 'executor') before the provider write, so exactly one caller reaches the provider and a loser reads back the winner's action_records row and returns its receipt with executed:false. The claim is RELEASED on a provider refusal (the repository already exposes that at :158) so a retry is a genuine retry, which is what v5 promised and could not deliver. (2) issueCapability takes an optional nonceSeed, and the approve route passes `apr:${approval_id}`, so two approves of the same row mint the SAME nonce and collapse onto the first receipt instead of writing twice. The executor's read of action_records still runs first, so a duplicate returns its receipt even while a kill switch is active.

MICRO-LIMITS SIT ABOVE EVERY SEEDED ACTION. v5 set budget-change's limit to 250_000_000 micros (₹250) — derived from, and then set below, the seed's own stated ₹300 downside (scripts/seed.js:182) — and never pinned the seeded intent's delta_micros, so the demo success path could fail MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. CORRECTED: the seed pins apr_seed_budget_1's stored intent constraints.delta_micros to 200_000_000 (₹200, inside the limit) and apr_seed_launch_1's to 0 (campaign-launch's limit is 0), and a seed-coherence test asserts every seeded approval's delta is at or under its class limit, so the demo can never be seeded into a gate it cannot pass.

RECONCILIATION IS SCOPED TO WRITES THAT CAN BE READ BACK. createDraft has no counterpart in READ_METHODS (src/integrations/meta_ads/index.js:41-46), so v5's 're-read through the read interface' step had nothing to re-read for a launch write. CORRECTED: the ACTION_METHOD contract marks each write with its read counterpart, and a write with none is documented and tested as reconciliation:'unknown' by contract rather than left to fail or to be quietly reported as reconciled.

v5's four earlier corrections are kept because they are right and I re-checked them: the executor owns the durable nonce dedupe and runs it first, while the kernel's injected port is read-only {seen} and owns REPLAYED_NONCE in isolation; the QA script runs the idempotency step before the guardian step so no step needs a live write under a freeze; the reset step is in-place (`npm run sdlc:seed -- --reset-approvals`) because the harness owns the boot (config.yml env.boot) and src/index.js holds the SQLite handle for the process lifetime, so unlinking data/app.db would leave the server on a deleted inode; and the seed carries exactly two pending fixtures with fixed ids and distinct classes.

ALSO CARRIED from v5: ACTION_CLASSES derived from DECISION_CLASSES (src/domain/decisions.js:21-26 freezes budget-change, campaign-status, creative-refresh, campaign-launch) with new-geography as the single explicit policy-only extension; the read path for a global-scope kill switch, with no '' sentinel, so repositories.js:4's every-query-binds-tenant_id contract keeps holding; pending-vs-lapsed as a read-time predicate so an aged row can never render in both the queue and the lapsed section; the five-state loading/error/partial early-returns in approvals() preserved verbatim so test/web/pages.test.js:55-63's /stale|await|Expired|provisional/i assertion still has something to match on an empty database; expiry clamped to min(ttlMs, approval.expires_at); docs/ui.md:35's typing-free explicit confirm, so approve is two-step; and src/web/client.js's false '<100 lines' header comment corrected to the real constraint.

A pending card whose class posture is shadow or no-evidence renders its approve button DISABLED with the same rule wording the kernel enforces, so the page can never invite an action the gate refuses. This is unreachable on the seed after the fixture fix above, which is exactly why it needs a test rather than a hope.

files.change: Pure domain module, no IO. ACTION_CLASSES is DERIVED from DECISION_CLASSES imported from src/domain/decisions.js and extended by exactly one explicit policy-only entry, new-geography; each class carries {microLimitMicros, requiredMaturityBand} and POLICY_ONLY_CLASSES is exported so a caller can label those rows policy-only rather than journal-representable. Limits in integer micros (TR-1): budget-change microLimitMicros 250_000_000 / requiredMaturityBand 'protective'; campaign-launch 0 / 'protective'; creative-refresh 0 / 'moderate'; campaign-status 0 / 'emergency-only' (a status flip moves no money and is the canonical emergency-band action, so the seeded demo's immature store does not by itself make the class unauthonomous); new-geography 0 / 'strategic'. validateIntent(intent, {nowIso, trust, approval, maturity}) -> {ok,intent}|{ok:false,error} is the ONLY place a capability can be minted, so it is where the trust gate lives. Order of its checks, and the order is the contract: (1) MALFORMED_INTENT — the action class is not on the roster; (2) AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED — resolve the posture from the injected `trust` value ('autonomous-under-micro-limits' | 'approval-required' | 'shadow' | 'no-evidence'): shadow and no-evidence are refused outright even with a valid approval, and approval-required is refused unless `approval` is a row for the same tenant and action class whose status is 'pending' and whose expires_at is in the future; a mismatched, terminal or expired approval is AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED too, with details naming which of the three failed; (3) MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED — constraints.delta_micros exceeds the class limit, checked as a safe non-negative integer and never coerced from a float or a numeric string; (4) MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED — AUTONOMOUS PATH ONLY, and FAIL CLOSED: an undefined, null or non-numeric `maturity` is blocked, never treated as 'no band to check', because a check that cannot read its input must not pass. The band is the autonomy gate and a human approval is the alternative authority for a class that has not earned autonomy (TR-7 read with TR-19): an approval-required class with a valid approval is governed by the human plus the micro-limit, and its band still stops it from ever becoming autonomous. Both directions are stated in the doc comment and pinned by a test. issueCapability(validated, {secret, policyVersion, ttlMs, nowIso, expiresAtCap, nonceSeed}) — the first argument is the {ok, intent} object validateIntent returns, NOT a bare intent, so a caller cannot sign something the kernel did not clear; it throws or rejects on anything else. Signs with node:crypto createHmac and timingSafeEqual and returns {tenant, resource, action, constraints, expiry, nonce, policy_version} plus a cap_-prefixed id; expiry is min(now+ttlMs, expiresAtCap) when a cap is passed, so a capability minted from an approval can never outlive it. When nonceSeed is given the nonce is derived deterministically from it (HMAC of seed+tenant+action+resource under the signing secret, hex-truncated), so two issuances of the SAME logical action collapse onto one nonce; without a seed the nonce is random. validateCapability(capability, {secret, nowIso, killSwitches, nonces}) -> {ok,capability}|{ok:false,error} with codes MALFORMED_CAPABILITY, BAD_SIGNATURE, EXPIRED_CAPABILITY, REPLAYED_NONCE, OVER_SCOPE (details name the violated constraint), KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE, MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED. Both ports are INJECTED and non-mutating: killSwitches {isActive(scope, scopeId)}, nonces {seen(nonce)} — seen, not claim; claiming a nonce is the executor's job, and this module must never reserve one. validateCapability deliberately does NOT consult trust: the capability is signed authority, and re-gating it against live ledger state at execution time would let a later ledger edit retroactively invalidate an issued capability. Imports no driver, provider, repository, sqlite or process.env; the secret arrives as an argument only.
files.why: One minter is the answer to the recorded rejection, and making issueCapability take validateIntent's return value is what turns that from a claim into a type the routes cannot get wrong. Deriving ACTION_CLASSES from DECISION_CLASSES is what stops this becoming the two-sources-of-truth failure src/domain/decisions.js:1-8 exists to prevent. One owner per nonce check is what makes AC-1 and AC-2 simultaneously satisfiable.

files.change: Pure. scoreFor(row) over a stored ledger row {evaluated, correct, needless, downside_penalties} and postureFor(actionClass, row) -> 'autonomous-under-micro-limits' | 'approval-required' | 'shadow' | 'no-evidence', with documented thresholds (autonomous requires >= 3 evaluated for that class, precision >= 0.90 and false-intervention rate <= 0.05), a pinned flag forcing shadow regardless of score, and the distinct value 'no-evidence' for a class with no row at all (TR-24, fail closed). files.why: TR-19 needs a per-class number, and one pure function over one stored ledger is what keeps the posture table and the gate on the same source. Naming the callers explicitly is the fix for the exact contradiction the rejection cited.

files.change: createExecutor({repositories, provider, kernel, auditClock}). The only module that calls a provider WRITE_METHOD. Deliberately takes NO trust parameter: the trust gate is at issuance (src/policy/kernel.js validateIntent) and this module's doc comment says so and points at it, so the two are not confused again. execute(capability, {actor}) runs its checks in THIS order, and the order is the contract: (1) DURABLE DEDUPE FIRST, in two sub-steps that together close the race v5 left open — (1a) read action_records by nonce and, if a receipt already exists, return {executed:false, receipt_id, reconciliation} immediately without validating through the kernel and without calling the provider; (1b) ATOMIC CLAIM: repositories.idempotency.claim(tenantId, nonce, 'executor') before any provider call, so of two racing deliveries exactly one proceeds; a false return means another caller won, so wait for its action_records row and return that winner's {executed:false, receipt_id, reconciliation} with no provider call. A duplicate delivery performs no mutation, so it returns its receipt even while a kill switch is active — stated in the doc comment so no one 'fixes' it into a 409. (2) kernel validateCapability, which is where KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE and the signature/expiry/scope rejections happen. (3) resolve the write method from the capability's SIGNED action through the contract module's ACTION_METHOD map (never from anything the caller passes at execute time) and call it on the injected provider. (4) re-read provider state through the read counterpart named for that write in the contract and classify drift (reported differs from applied; source 'manual'|'platform'|'third-party' as the provider reports it, 'none' when they agree); a write with NO read counterpart — createDraft — returns reconciliation:'unknown' by contract rather than inventing a value or reporting a reconciliation it cannot compute, and this is documented on the contract, not only in the executor. (5) append the action_records receipt and an audit event carrying actor and capability id, then RELEASE the claim; return {executed:true, receipt_id, requested, reported, reconciliation, drift}. A provider refusal (ok:false) releases the claim via the repository's release (src/data/repositories.js:158), returns {executed:false, error, reconciliation:'unknown'}, writes NO action_records row, and leaves the caller's approval pending, so a retry is a genuine retry rather than a silently swallowed claim. The provider is injected per request; the executor never constructs one.
files.why: Durable nonce state lives in the repository the executor already writes, not in the per-request fake (src/api/routes.js builds a new one per request, so a fake-side dedupe could not survive the two deliveries AC-2 describes). Using the repo's own claim primitive rather than get-then-act is what makes the guarantee hold under two racing requests, and the release-on-refusal is what keeps 'a retry is a genuine retry' true.

The autonomy gate's placement at issuance rather than execution is a design argument, not a spec quotation: a signed capability is authority, and re-gating it on live ledger state at execution time would let a later ledger edit retroactively invalidate a capability a human already approved. A plan that can be wrong in that many mutually reinforcing ways deserves humility even after the corrections, and the implementer will be following text no proposer has validated. The other drag is unchanged and irreducible here: the maturity-band reading is an interpretation of TR-7 rather than a quotation, the autonomy the demo exercises is seeded rather than earned, and the drift source is asserted against a fake that reports whatever simulateDrift is told. What would move this up: implementing test/policy/kernel.test.js and the two racing-delivery cases in test/executor/executor.test.js first and seeing the gate hold across all four postures with the atomic claim closing the race. What would move it down: a reviewer rejecting the band reading, since AC-4's autonomous case and AC-5's approval case both run through it, or the seed's approval-required row being wrong in a way that makes the demo unapprovable again.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right about the diagnosis and right about four things that would have shipped broken, so most of it is folded in. I want to be specific about the disagreement, because the proposal and the critique were not equally right and neither was tidy. The critique's two BLOCKING findings are real and I confirmed both against v5's own text rather than taking them on trust. First: v5 claimed validateIntent was the only place a capability could be minted, and then specified the approve route resolving the posture itself, refusing only 'not shadow', and calling issueCapability directly — so the gate had two owners and the one that escaped was the human-approval path, the money-moving one, which skipped the micro-limit, the band and the no-evidence refusal. That is the exact defect the previous rejection was about, one layer down: v4 was caught shipping a ledger enforced by nothing, and v5 was caught shipping a gate the money path walked around. The fix is structural rather than textual — a shared issuance helper both routes call, plus issueCapability taking validateIntent's return object so a route cannot sign an unvalidated intent even by accident, plus a boundary test that pins the call sites. Second: v5 seeded its failure-path fixture as campaign-launch with no ledger row, which its own gate refuses outright, so AC-5's 502 reconciliation panel and the QA step that produces it were unreachable through the gate it had just built. One seeded ledger row fixes it, and it also lets me keep the no-evidence demonstration on creative-refresh where it costs nothing. I took the three MAJOR findings too: the band gate was wired to nothing and failed open on an undefined maturity (the fix reuses maturityFor/policyBand, already imported at routes.js:16/19 — one line of reuse, not new machinery), and validateIntent now fails closed on an unreadable input; budget-change's 250,000,000 limit sat below the seed's own 300,000,000 figure at scripts/seed.js:182 with the fixture's delta never pinned, which could break the demo's own success path; and the dedupe was get-then-act while the repo already ships the single-winner primitive the plan never used. I took the MINOR finding on createDraft having no read counterpart, and folded it as a contract property with a test rather than a comment. I also took the edge case the proposal missed entirely — a pending card whose class is shadow renders a live Approve button the gate will refuse — because the page and the gate must not disagree in the same way the plan contradicted itself twice. What I REJECTED, explicitly: the critique's suggestion to give some class a requiredMaturityBand above the seeded store's band 'so the gate is demonstrably live'. campaign-status is the only class the seed calibrates autonomous, so raising its band makes the autonomous path fail MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED and IAC-4's live case unobservable. The honest move is to wire the gate correctly and say in residual_risks that the demo does not exercise it, which I have done; a demo that demonstrates itself by refusing to run is not a demonstration. I also rejected its alternative of dropping MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED entirely — TR-7 is in this issue's coverage list, and a roster the kernel does not gate is the same display-only defect one field over. I rejected its framing of the idempotency finding as a demand to re-key on approval id: that is the right instinct for the approval path and I folded it in as a deterministic nonce seed, but as a REPLACEMENT for the nonce it would break AC-2, whose duplicate is the same capability posted twice with no approval in the request at all. The two are complementary and the work order now carries both. Two more of its edge cases I declined to turn into design changes: the in-flight freeze straddle is unreachable while the fake's writes are synchronous and belongs with the real write path, and the unicode round-trip is already covered by the escaped-copy assertion, which I extended to include the two-step confirm state rather than treating as a new gap. I did not simply accept the critique's severity ordering either: the two blocking findings are load-bearing for the recorded rejection, the band and idempotency findings are real but do not defeat a criterion on their own, and the createDraft one is a contract statement. Separately, BOTH documents missed something and I am recording it rather than leaving it to a reviewer: v5's AC-2 says 'qa_script step 7' for the idempotency step and AC-5 says 'steps 5-6' for the two approvals, but the script has nine steps and those are steps 8 and 6-7 — the same unrenumbered-pointer error v3 was corrected for, reappearing after the script grew. I have removed the numeric pointers from the acceptance criteria entirely and named each step by its content, so a future edit to the script cannot silently invalidate a criterion. The proposal's own unknowns stay unresolved and I have not dressed them up: the capability-issuance surface is unauthenticated, the drift source is fake-only, and the live Meta mutation surface is unread by design.

validated_work_order.approach:
Build the write path as six new tables behind one additive migration, four new pure-or-injected modules, one new domain module, and one composition point, then make every existing consumer of approval, posture or maturity state read through a single definition of each.

1. src/data/db.js adds migration 006 and two PRAGMAs. WAL and busy_timeout go in openDatabase, not in a route: busy_timeout is per-connection, and both the server and the seed process open through this one function, so that is the only place the setting reaches both.
2. src/data/repositories.js adds six repositories behind the same tenant-bound module contract (repositories.js:1-7): approvals (mutable working state, like experiments), capabilities (append-only), actionRecords (append-only on UPDATE, DELETE deliberately allowed - the only reason is named in db.js), killSwitches (mutable), guardianIncidents (append-only), trustLedger (mutable upsert).
3. src/domain/approvals.js is pure: validateApproval, visibleReason, isPendingApproval, partitionApprovals. One predicate decides pending versus lapsed, and four callers (the decide route, the page, the seed reset and the tests) read it instead of four implementations of it.
4. src/policy/kernel.js is the deterministic gate and the only place a write is admitted. Its roster is derived from DECISION_CLASSES by membership and its own render order is pinned, the maturity band is a FLOOR in the direction policyBand's edges already encode, the intent's action is bound to the class that registers it, capabilities are HMAC-signed, and the kill-switch check names the four scope keys it evaluates.
5. src/policy/trust.js derives one posture per class from one stored ledger row and is called by BOTH the rendered table and the gate, so the displayed posture and the enforced posture cannot disagree.
6. src/executor/executor.js is the only module that calls a provider write method, and it dedupes durably in the repository rather than in the per-request fake, which is rebuilt on every request (routes.js:103) and could not survive a second delivery.
7. src/strategy/guardian.js holds the two detectors, the named recovery predicate and the freeze, and freeze takes an explicit scope and scopeId across the four levels the issue names.
8. src/api/routes.js is the composition point and the only place maturity is computed: one helper, extracted from GET /v1/metrics, now called by the metric route and by both issuance routes, and ONE providerForRequest helper is the single source of a request's failure injection for every write route.
9. src/web/pages.js stops being a shell, and src/web/client.js grows the decide fetch, the three-way response branch and the re-decide control.
10. scripts/seed.js writes four approval fixtures, five trust rows and a --reset-approvals affordance whose nonce list is built by CALLING decisionNonce over the same seeded id list, so no prefix literal is ever written twice.

THREE RULES CARRY THE WHOLE PLAN. A PREFIX LITERAL CANNOT DRIFT IF IT IS NEVER WRITTEN: decisionNonce is the single definition and both the decide route and the reset call it. A PREDICATE CANNOT BE DISAGREED WITH IF IT IS WRITTEN ONCE: isPendingApproval has four callers and one body, the roster is one exported array with two assertions over it (set equality with DECISION_CLASSES, and its pinned order), and killSwitches.activeFor answers for every scope the same way the write side writes them. And EVERY ASSERTION A QA READER COMPARES LITERALLY HAS A NAMED MECHANISM BEHIND IT: a method, a response field, a selector or a URL - which is the defect class the last four rounds each rejected, and the rule applied to every line of qa_script below.

Pure, no IO, no repository import. validateApproval(approval) rejects an action_class outside ACTION_CLASSES, a non-UTC or unparseable expires_at, a missing or blank impact or downside, and a constraints.delta_micros that is not a non-negative safe integer.

visibleReason(value) -> string|null. Trim, reject null, empty and whitespace, reject over 500 characters with REASON_TOO_LONG, and strip the invisible set [\\u200B-\\u200D\\u2060\\uFEFF] before the emptiness check so a zero-width-space-only reason is rejected the same way an empty one is. It then also requires at least one character that survives removing whitespace, the invisible set, and Unicode combining marks (\p{M}), because a reason made only of combining marks passes trim() and the client's identical check and then renders as an empty-looking input while the audit row records something. The stripped and trimmed text is what is stored, verbatim, and escapeHtml handles it on render.

isPendingApproval(row, {nowIso}) is THE predicate: status === 'pending' AND Date.parse(expires_at) > Date.parse(nowIso). An expires_at exactly equal to nowIso is NOT pending. Four consumers, one body: the decide route's rule (2), pages.js's partition, the seed reset's own reasoning, and the test counts.

partitionApprovals(rows, {nowIso}) -> {pending, executed, rejected, lapsed}, each bucket ordered (expires_at, approval_id) so the page is deterministic. 'lapsed' is a status of 'pending' whose expires_at is at or before nowIso - it is derived, never stored. NOTE WHAT THIS RETURNS AND DOES NOT: it buckets APPROVAL rows, so it cannot carry a receipt id, a reconciliation or a drift, because the approvals table has no such columns. The executed-receipts panel is therefore NOT driven by the executed bucket of this function; it is driven by repositories.actionRecords, and pages.js joins the two by approval_id. Stated here so the next reader does not try to render a receipt from a bucket that has none.

Each entry carries {microLimitMicros, requiresMicrosConstraint, requiredMaturityBand, action}: campaign-status {50_000_000, constraint NOT permitted, 'emergency-only', set_campaign_status}; budget-change {50_000_000, micros REQUIRED, 'emergency-only', update_campaign_budget}; creative-refresh {10_000_000, not permitted, 'emergency-only', update_campaign_creative}; new-geography {0, not permitted, 'emergency-only', create_campaign, policy-only}; campaign-launch {0, not permitted, 'emergency-only', create_campaign}. POLICY_ONLY_CLASSES = ['new-geography'] so a caller can label a policy-only row.

decisionNonce(approvalId) -> 'apr_' + approvalId. THE SINGLE DEFINITION of the approval-decision nonce in the repository. The prefix literal appears inside this function and nowhere else. The decide route calls decisionNonce(approvalId); the seed reset builds its list by SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS.map(decisionNonce); nothing writes 'apr_' or 'apr_seed_' by hand. test/policy/kernel.test.js pins the value with one assertion. Consequence to state plainly: the reset's deletion predicate is NOT a prefix match. It is a WHERE tenant_id = ? AND nonce IN (<that mapped list>), so it cannot disagree with the value the approve path stores whatever a later slice renames a fixture to.

validateIntent(intent, {nowIso, posture, approval, maturity}) -> {ok, intent} | {ok:false, error}. THE AUTONOMY GATE and the only place a write is admitted. Rules IN THIS ORDER, and the order is part of the contract - a class refused for want of an approval must never reach the band check.
  (a) intent.action_class must be in the roster, else AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED with details.reason 'unknown-class'.
  (a2) intent.action must EQUAL the action the roster registers for that class, else AUTONOMY_NOT_EARNED with details.reason 'action-mismatch'. This sits BEFORE every approval rule. Without it the calibration story is unenforced at the only place it is enforced: the seed earns autonomy for campaign-status on a reversible action, and a caller posts {action_class:'campaign-status', action:'create_campaign'} and receives a signed envelope for a campaign creation under a posture the ledger never granted for anything irreversible. The two available enforcement points are refuse-the-mismatch and silently-overwrite-the-envelope-action. THIS PLAN PINS REFUSE, so a mis-paired intent is a visible 403 with a named reason. The test names campaign-status carrying create_campaign as the case that must fail.
  (b) A missing or unrecognised posture is a REFUSAL, never a default, and a malformed approval row is a refusal. Every ambiguous input fails closed (TR-24).
  (c) posture 'autonomous-under-micro-limits' with approval === null admits.
  (d) The SAME posture WITH an approval row present is ALSO ADMITTED, because an approval is additional authority and never a disqualifier, but the row is still validated when present, so one that does not cover this intent is refused with details.reason 'mismatch' (different action_class or resource), 'terminal' (status executed or rejected) or 'expired' (expires_at <= nowIso). Rule (d) exists because approving a class the seed calibrates autonomous is a real case, and leaving it undefined is how a wrong write happens in the highest-risk slice in the project.
  (e) ANY other posture ('approval-required', 'shadow', or the fail-closed no-row default) admits ONLY with an approval row present, unexpired at nowIso, non-terminal, and matching intent.action_class and intent.resource; otherwise the refusal names the failing condition 'no-approval', 'expired', 'terminal' or 'mismatch'. 'shadow' is IN this rule deliberately: shadow means NEVER AUTONOMOUS, not never possible. A human approval is the whole point of the approvals queue, and a reading in which a shadow-pinned class can never be approved makes the queue a dead end for the highest-risk class the product knows. IAC-4 asks that new-geography 'stays in shadow or approval', which is exactly this split.
  (f) THE MICRO-LIMIT, THEN THE BAND. MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED when the intent's amount exceeds the class microLimitMicros, where the amount is constraints.delta_micros when it is a finite number and 0 otherwise. THE COMPARISON FOR A CLASS THAT DOES NOT REQUIRE A MICROS CONSTRAINT IS STATED BECAUSE A CRITERION RESTS ON IT: an absent constraints.delta_micros is 0 and the check is 0 <= microLimitMicros, so campaign-status with an empty constraints object is admitted, while a NEGATIVE delta_micros is MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED on every class regardless of the flag. For budget-change, whose requiresMicrosConstraint is true, an absent, non-numeric, negative or non-integer delta_micros is ALSO MICRO_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, because a missing number is not a small number and an absent constraint otherwise passes an upper-bound check by not existing.

RULE (f)'s BAND IS A FLOOR AND ITS DIRECTION IS NOT NEGOTIABLE. The intent's band is policyBand(maturity).label and the class's requiredMaturityBand is the LOWEST band permitted to act: admit iff BAND_ORDER.indexOf(actual) >= BAND_ORDER.indexOf(required), where BAND_ORDER = ['emergency-only','protective','moderate','strategic'] and labelFor(band) is exported alongside. policyBand is IMPORTED from src/domain/measurement.js rather than restated, and BAND_ORDER is the order its <0.35 / <0.70 / <0.90 edges already encode, so the gate and the metric surface cannot drift apart. A HIGHER band NEVER blocks: a class requiring 'protective' is ADMITTED at maturity 0.95, and a class requiring 'strategic' is refused for every maturity below 0.90, which coincides with policyBand's own gated flag. maturity 0.90 exactly is 'strategic' and is admitted, matching test/domain/measurement.test.js:106. A CEILING reading inverts the safety property: it would admit data at maturity 0 that the class declared too immature and refuse data at 0.95 that it declared ready. Note the doc drift, do not inherit it: docs/trd.md's TR-7 line writes '>0.90 strategic' where src/domain/measurement.js:244-259 and its pinned test say '>= 0.90'. The implementation wins, docs/ is out of bounds from a ticket branch, and the drift is filed in out_of_scope.

THE MATURITY ARGUMENT IS VALIDATED BEFORE IT IS USED, AND null IS ONE OF THE BAD VALUES. Anything that is not a finite number (undefined, null, NaN, a numeric string) is refused MATURITY_BAND_BLOCKED with details {required, actual: null, maturity: null, reason: 'maturity-unknown'} BEFORE policyBand is called. null is explicitly in that set because the route's own computation substitutes 0 for a tenant with no events, and laundering 'no evidence' into a legitimate 0 is the same fail-open by a different door. maturity is a caller-supplied number and never an internal read: this module never touches a repository or a clock, so the ROUTE that supplies it owns the source and the doc comment says so.

issueCapability(intent, {secret, policyVersion, ttlMs, nowIso, expiresAtCap, nonce}) signs with node:crypto createHmac and returns {tenant, resource, action, constraints, maturity, band, expiry, nonce, policy_version} plus a capability_id, with expiry = min(now + ttlMs, expiresAtCap) and ttlMs 900_000. THE ENVELOPE CARRIES maturity AND band because they are properties of the gate decision and signing them is what makes the receipt's audit columns trustworthy: the executor copies them onto the action_records row, so the receipt records the band that was actually enforced on BOTH the autonomous and the approval path rather than null on the autonomous one. nonce is OPTIONAL and generated internally ('nce_' + 16 hex from randomUUID) only when omitted, which is what lets the decide route pass decisionNonce(approvalId) instead of a string it assembles itself.

validateCapability(capability, {secret, nowIso, killSwitches, nonces}) -> MALFORMED_CAPABILITY, BAD_SIGNATURE, EXPIRED_CAPABILITY, REPLAYED_NONCE, OVER_SCOPE (details name the violated constraint), KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE. Both injected ports are NON-MUTATING and read-only: killSwitches {isActive(tenantId, scope, scopeId)} and nonces {seen(tenantId, nonce)} where seen is never claim, because claiming a nonce is the executor's job and this module must never reserve one. createKernel({secret, policyVersion, ttlMs, killSwitches, nonces}) binds the ports and has the routes as their only callers. THE nonces PORT IS BOUND TO action_records, NOT TO capabilities: action_records carries UNIQUE (tenant_id, nonce) and holds a row only after a successful write, so seen is false for a freshly issued capability and true only for a nonce already spent. Binding it to capabilities would make seen true for every capability and validateCapability would answer REPLAYED_NONCE on every execution. REPLAYED_NONCE is therefore defence in depth that the executor's earlier dedupe shadows on the live path; the doc comment says so, and no one should 'fix' the duplicate answer into a 409 to make the branch reachable.

THE KILL-SWITCH CHECK, EXPLICITLY, because leaving it implicit is what made KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE and OVER_SCOPE unobservable: validateCapability evaluates FOUR scope keys, in this order, and refuses on the FIRST active one with details {scope, scope_id}. The keys are, and every one is derivable from the signed envelope with nothing added to it: ('global', envelope.tenant) - a global freeze is stored under the tenant that raised it, never under a '' sentinel - ('tenant', envelope.tenant), ('provider', 'meta_ads') - the sole provider this epic integrates, named as a constant here so the string is written once - and ('campaign', envelope.resource). A write is refused if any of the four is active, so a provider-wide freeze blocks a campaign write and a campaign-wide freeze blocks only that campaign. OVER_SCOPE is the sibling refusal and is what keeps a tenant's envelope from being executed against another tenant's resource: it is the combination of envelope.tenant not matching the caller's tenantId and a scope check that the envelope names. POSTURE_LABELS maps the three machine postures to the display strings the page renders and the criterion quotes: 'autonomous under micro-limits', 'approval required', 'shadow'.

Pure, no IO, no repository import. scoreFor(row) over a stored ledger row {evaluated, correct, needless, downside_penalties} and postureFor(actionClass, row, roster, pinned) -> 'autonomous-under-micro-limits' | 'approval-required' | 'shadow', with documented thresholds: autonomous requires evaluated >= 3 for that class AND precision (correct/evaluated) >= 0.90 AND false-intervention rate (needless/evaluated) <= 0.05 AND downside_penalties === 0. A pinned flag forces 'shadow' regardless of score, and a class with NO row is 'approval-required' (TR-24, fail closed), which is the only other path to that label and the reason the campaign-launch row of the table carries the 'no evidence' Why copy. recordOutcome(row, {outcome, needless, downside}) folds one evaluation into the next row. The two callers are the approvals page's posture table and kernel.validateIntent, both calling this one function, so the displayed posture and the enforced posture cannot disagree. The executor does NOT call it and must not: a signed capability is the attestation, and re-deriving posture at execute time would let a later trust-row edit retroactively invalidate a correctly issued capability.

createExecutor({repositories, provider, kernel, auditClock}). The ONLY module that calls a provider write method. execute(capability, {actor, tenantId}) runs its checks in THIS ORDER and the order is the contract.

(0) TENANT. The capability's own tenant field must equal the caller's tenantId, else {executed:false, error:{code:'TENANT_MISMATCH'}} with no write; the envelope is bearer material and the executor does not take the caller's word for it.

(1) DURABLE DEDUPE FIRST, in two sub-steps. (1a) If actionRecords.getByNonce(tenantId, nonce) already holds a row, return {executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id, reconciliation, drift} immediately, without validating through the kernel and without calling the provider; a duplicate mutates nothing, so it returns its receipt even while a kill switch is active. Stated in the doc comment so nobody 'fixes' it into a 409, because a second tab or a retried POST is exactly the case where a 409 tells the operator their action failed when it succeeded. (1b) ATOMIC CLAIM, repositories.idempotency.claim(tenantId, nonce, 'executor') before the provider call, using the primitive the repository already ships (:133-172, whose claim is INSERT OR IGNORE and so genuinely atomic, and the shape src/workflows/scheduler.js:71-79 already uses), so of two interleaved deliveries exactly one reaches the provider; a false return means another caller won, so return {executed:false, duplicate:false, error:{code:'EXECUTION_IN_PROGRESS', retryable:true}} with NO provider call and NO wait. Step 1a alone is check-then-act and does not close the two-tab race; 1b is what makes that claim true. The loser is told to retry rather than to wait on a receipt row, because a winner that then FAILS releases the claim (below) and no row is ever coming - a bounded wait on a row that may never appear is the trap this replaces.

(2) kernel.validateCapability, where the signature, expiry, scope, replay and kill-switch rejections happen, the last over the four scope keys named in the kernel entry. ANY REFUSAL HERE, AND ANY REFUSAL FROM (0), RELEASES the 1b CLAIM through repositories.idempotency.release(tenantId, nonce, 'executor') before returning. Nothing that did not reach the provider may leave a nonce burned.

(3) Resolve the write method from the capability's SIGNED action through the contract module's ACTION_WRITES map, never from anything the caller passes at execute time, and derive its arguments from the envelope through ONE named function, writeArgsFor(action, envelope). resource supplies the target id for update and status actions - the adset id for update_campaign_budget, the campaign id for set_campaign_status and update_campaign_creative. For create_campaign the resource is a PROPOSED id that does not exist yet and the name comes from envelope.constraints.name, NOT from resource: createCampaign takes {name} and mints its own id, so reading the name off resource would create a campaign literally called 'campaign_004'. constraints supply delta_micros for the budget action and the target status for the status action. This is stated because a previous revision left the mapping unsaid and an implementer then wrote a create against a resource the fake's fixtures do not contain. The SAME provider instance serves the write and the re-read in (4), so one request reconciles against the state it just wrote.

(4) Re-read provider state through the read interface. drift is classified: 'none' when the re-read agrees with the request and the provider reported no drift, otherwise the source the provider itself reports - 'manual', 'platform' or 'third-party'. reconciliation is a CLOSED VOCABULARY with the same treatment, because the receipt column, the toast and the failure panel all render it and only one of its values was ever named: 'agreed' when the post-write re-read reports exactly the requested state, 'diverged' when the re-read succeeded and reports something else, 'partial' when only some of a multi-field change landed, and 'unknown' when there is no re-read to compare against. The success path therefore yields 'agreed' on seeded data, which is the string qa_script step 3 and the successful-approve test case quote; 'unknown' is the provider-refusal value and the only one that reaches the failure panel. The fake reports drift only from a writeDrift option the tests inject, so 'none' is the only drift value reachable in a live QA run; that is filed in residual_risks rather than implied to be covered.

(5) Append the action_records receipt (repositories.actionRecords.append), record the idempotency effect, append an audit event carrying actor and capability id, and return {executed:true, receipt_id, requested, reported, reconciliation, drift}. THE RECEIPT COPIES maturity AND band FROM THE ENVELOPE onto maturity_at_decision and band_at_decision, which is why those columns are signed rather than recomputed: without this the two audit columns are null on every autonomous receipt and the receipt cannot answer which band was enforced.

A provider refusal (ok:false) RELEASES the claim through repositories.idempotency.release, returns {executed:false, duplicate:false, error, reconciliation:'unknown'}, writes NO action_records row and claims no nonce durably, so the caller's approval stays pending and a retry is a genuine retry rather than a swallowed claim. The provider is injected per request; the executor never constructs one. This module does not import trust.js and does not consult the ledger: a signed capability is the attestation and the gate has one owner.

Three exported pure functions and two effects, all over deterministic fixtures.

DETECTORS. spendSpike(fixture, {nowIso}) compares observed spend micros over the window against the seeded baseline; trackingLoss(fixture, {nowIso}) reports no qualified event past STALE_THRESHOLD_HOURS, IMPORTED from src/domain/measurement.js:242 and not restated; evaluate(fixture, {nowIso}) dispatches on kind and returns {tripped, kind, details}. The two fixtures are exported from here so the trigger route, the tests and the page read one set.

RECOVERY PREDICATE, NAMED AND EXPORTED, because an earlier revision invoked 'the deterministic recovery predicate' without ever defining it. recoveryHolds(fixture, {nowIso, kind}) is the INVERSE of the matching detector: true exactly when evaluate() does not trip, so for spend-spike it is 'observed spend over the window is at or below the seeded baseline' and for tracking-loss it is 'a qualified event exists within STALE_THRESHOLD_HOURS'. The human half is the live route's job; the deterministic half is this function's.

freeze({repositories, tenantId, kind, details, actor, scope = 'provider', scopeId = 'meta_ads'}) writes the kill-switch row with the REAL resolved tenant_id, never a '' global sentinel, since every query in repositories.js:1-7 binds tenant_id. THE SCOPE PARAMETER EXISTS BECAUSE THE ISSUE NAMES FOUR LEVELS (global, tenant, provider, campaign) AND A SIGNATURE THAT COULD WRITE ONLY ONE DID NOT COVER THEM: scope is one of those four and scope_id is the corresponding id. The default is the provider scope because the demo's only provider is Meta Ads, and it is safe to default to a non-global scope ONLY because killSwitches.activeFor returns every active row for the tenant whatever its scope - the read side was widened to match the write side in the same change, and a test asserts the two agree, so the default can never quietly produce a row no reader can see. It also appends a guardian_incidents row and an audit event through repositories.auditEvents.append({tenant_id, actor, action, subject, details}). Incidents are append-only and never updated: current state is the join with the kill switch, and the banner's kind reads the newest incident by (frozen_at, incident_id), a documented tiebreak because two incidents can share a frozen_at.

reEnable({repositories, tenantId, scope = 'provider', scopeId = 'meta_ads', actor}) REQUIRES an explicit human actor, and with none it is refused RE_ENABLE_ACTOR_REQUIRED. The scope and scopeId defaults are THE SAME LITERALS freeze defaults to, and they are declared here rather than in the route so the two can be compared by a test: a re-enable that named no scope must clear the row the demo's trigger wrote, and a re-enable whose scope does not match the frozen row's clears nothing and reports success, which is the failure mode this default removes. It clears the row and appends an audit event. It does NOT take a recovery predicate.

The ONE documented exception to the actor requirement is resetSeededKillSwitches(tenantId), which clears exactly the row a live trigger writes - scope 'provider', scope_id 'meta_ads' for that tenant - is called only by scripts/seed.js --reset-approvals and is reachable from no route, so the live re-enable path keeps its human-actor invariant.

Beside READ_METHODS (:41-46), add the write half of the provider interface and the one map the executor resolves through. WRITE_METHODS = Object.freeze(['setCampaignStatus', 'updateAdSetBudget', 'updateCampaignCreative', 'createCampaign']) - the four actions ACTION_CLASSES registers, and no more. ACTION_WRITES is a frozen object mapping each registered action name to its method: set_campaign_status -> setCampaignStatus, update_campaign_budget -> updateAdSetBudget, update_campaign_creative -> updateCampaignCreative, create_campaign -> createCampaign. It is keyed by the CONTRACT'S action slugs, not by the JS method names, because the executor looks it up with the capability's SIGNED action string. An action absent from the map is a MALFORMED_CAPABILITY, not a fallthrough to a default. Every write returns the same {ok, ...} envelope the reads use, so the executor has one failure shape to handle: {ok:true, data} on success and {ok:false, error:{code, message, details}} on refusal, with the same codes the read path already returns (META_ERROR_PARAMS' FAILURE_MODES plus the provider's own).

The four WRITE_METHODS, against a per-instance deep copy of FIXTURES rather than the module constant, so a write in one request is not visible in the next - which is what makes AC-2's 'executes exactly once' observable only through the durable store and never through the provider, exactly as the routes.js:103 per-request construction implies. RULES FOR THE WRITES, each one matching a domain rule rather than a convenience: money stays in integer micros, so updateAdSetBudget refuses a non-integer or negative delta_micros and never divides; setCampaignStatus accepts only ACTIVE|PAUSED and the change is visible to the next read on the SAME instance; createCampaign takes {name}, mints the next campaign_00N id, and returns a PAUSED campaign (a new campaign is never born ACTIVE); updateCampaignCreative replaces the creative's name on the named campaign and refuses a campaign the instance does not hold. failureMode applies to WRITES on the same terms as it already applies to reads (:99-115) - quota and revoked refuse with the same codes, messages and simulated details - because the ?meta_error browser clause is a write-path clause and a fake that only failed on reads could not produce it. The deterministic by-id sort the reads already use is applied to every list the writes can change, since FIXTURES is declared out of id order on purpose (:22-25) and a write that appended unsorted would break the contract suite's existing id-order assertion. live.js is NOT required to implement the write interface in this slice and gains no write method: the seam is typed and the live adapter is a later slice, so nothing here commits to a live write contract.

The composition point, and the only place maturity is computed. buildApp gains three optional parameters with pinned defaults - buildApp({repositories, policySecret = DEFAULT_SIGNING_SECRET, policyVersion = '1', capabilityTtlMs = 900_000}) - so the ten existing buildApp call sites (src/index.js:19, test/api/*.test.js, test/web/pages.test.js:227,275,393, test/web/drawer.test.js:22) keep working untouched and a test that needs to forge can pass its own secret. The signing literal is NOT in this file; kernel.js holds it and this file imports DEFAULT_SIGNING_SECRET from there.

ONE PROVIDER HELPER, BECAUSE THE FAILURE-INJECTION CONVENTION MUST NOT BE APPLIED TO ONE WRITE ROUTE AND FORGOTTEN ON THE NEXT. providerForRequest(request) -> new FakeMetaAdsProvider({failureMode: META_ERROR_PARAMS.has(request.query.meta_error) ? request.query.meta_error : 'ok'}), defined once at module level next to META_ERROR_PARAMS (:37). The existing page loop (:100-102) is refactored to call it, and BOTH write routes - POST /v1/approvals/:approvalId/approve and POST /v1/actions/execute - call it and nothing else. This is the defect class the last four rounds each rejected, recurring at a new site: the previous revision named the failureMode source for the execute route and left the approve route saying only 'a provider built for this request', so an implementer following it literally builds the approve route's provider with the default 'ok', the write succeeds, and the failure half of AC-5 can never be observed in a browser - the criterion the recorded rejection was about.

MATURITY, EXTRACTED ONCE. A module-level helper tenantMaturity(repositories, tenantId, nowIso) -> {maturity, band, data_through}, computed from repositories.rawEvents.listByTypes(tenantId, FUNNEL_TYPES) (:43) through dataThrough/maturityFor/policyBand exactly as GET /v1/metrics computes it today (:165-190), with ONE change: a tenant with no events returns maturity: null rather than the 0 the ternary at :174 substitutes. GET /v1/metrics keeps its current wire shape byte for byte by reporting `maturity: maturity ?? 0` and `band: policyBand(maturity ?? 0).label` explicitly, with a comment saying the display surface shows 0 for no data while the gate does not - and test/api/actions.test.js asserts both halves of that in one case, so the two surfaces cannot quietly converge or quietly diverge.

NEW ROUTES, in the order they are mounted (all under the existing app.use('/v1', express.json({strict:true})) at :124, so the 404 envelope at :492-494 still answers anything else):
  POST /v1/capabilities - body {tenant_id, action_class, action, resource, constraints}. Resolves the tenant, builds the intent, calls kernel.validateIntent with {posture: trust.postureFor(...), approval: null, maturity: tenantMaturity(...).maturity} and NOTHING ELSE may mint a capability. 201 {capability_id, envelope, expiry}. A refusal is 403 with the kernel's code and details.
  POST /v1/approvals/:approvalId/approve - the rules run in THIS ORDER, and the order is the contract:
    (0) REDELIVERY. If actionRecords.getByNonce(tenantId, decisionNonce(approvalId)) holds a row, answer 200 {approval_id, status:'executed', executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id, reconciliation, drift} and STOP. This rule is FIRST and is deliberately outside the gate: validateIntent refuses an approval row whose status is 'executed' as terminal (kernel rule d), so a duplicate resolved after the gate would 403 forever and the browser clause could never be observed. It is not a second owner of the gate because it mints nothing, issues no capability, calls no provider and mutates no row - it answers about a receipt that already exists. Its doc comment says exactly that. This is the clause the recorded objection required.
    (1) REASON. visibleReason(body.reason) must be a non-null string, else 400 REASON_REQUIRED.
    (2) THE ROW. repositories.approvals.get(tenantId, approvalId), else 404 APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND; isPendingApproval(row, {nowIso}) must hold, else 409 APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING with details.status naming the row's real status and whether it lapsed. The tenant comes from body.tenant_id or the row's own tenant, so the page sends what it rendered and a cross-tenant id 404s here rather than executing somebody else's approval.
    (3) THE GATE. kernel.validateIntent with the approval row supplied, exactly as POST /v1/capabilities does; a refusal is 403 with the kernel's code.
    (4) ISSUE AND EXECUTE. issueCapability with nonce: decisionNonce(approvalId) and expiresAtCap: row.expires_at, stored through repositories.capabilities.create, then executor.execute with the provider from providerForRequest(request) - THE SAME HELPER THE EXECUTE ROUTE USES, named here so the omission that broke AC-5 cannot recur.
    (5) PERSIST. A provider refusal answers 200 {approval_id, status:'pending', executed:false, duplicate:false, outcome:'provider_refused', error, reconciliation:'unknown'} and writes NO status change - the item stays pending, which is what the criterion asserts. A kill switch answers 409 {code:'KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE'}. A success answers 200 {approval_id, status:'executed', executed:true, receipt_id, reconciliation, drift, band, maturity} and calls repositories.approvals.decide(..., {status:'executed', reason, actor, decided_at}).
  POST /v1/approvals/:approvalId/reject - visibleReason, then the row must be pending (else the same 409), then repositories.approvals.decide(..., {status:'rejected', reason, actor, decided_at}) and 200 {approval_id, status:'rejected', decided:true}. It never mints a capability and never touches the executor, so a rejection cannot fail.
  POST /v1/actions/execute - body is a signed envelope. Builds ONE provider through providerForRequest(request) and passes that one instance to the executor for both the write and the re-read. The executor's result maps to HTTP: executed:true -> 200 with the receipt; duplicate -> 200 {executed:false, duplicate:true, receipt_id}; EXECUTION_IN_PROGRESS -> 409 with retryable:true; KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE -> 409; MALFORMED_CAPABILITY -> 400; BAD_SIGNATURE, EXPIRED_CAPABILITY, OVER_SCOPE, TENANT_MISMATCH -> 403.
  POST /v1/guardian/trigger?kind=spend-spike|tracking-loss - runs guardian.evaluate on the tenant's deterministic fixture, and when it trips calls guardian.freeze with the RESOLVED scope (body.scope, body.scope_id, defaulting to guardian.freeze's own defaults, ('provider','meta_ads')). 201 {frozen:true, scope, scope_id, kind, incidents}. An unknown kind is 400 GUARDIAN_KIND_UNKNOWN. It re-arms: a second POST after a re-enable writes the SAME row through the ON CONFLICT upsert and re-freezes, with no database reset, which is what the criterion needs on a re-check.
  POST /v1/guardian/re-enable - body {actor, scope, scope_id}; a missing or blank actor is 400 RE_ENABLE_ACTOR_REQUIRED before any write; a missing or blank scope or scope_id falls back to guardian.reEnable's own defaults, which are the same literals freeze defaults to, so a re-enable that names no scope clears the row the demo's trigger wrote. 200 {re_enabled:true, scope, scope_id}. The response echoes the RESOLVED scope rather than the requested one, so a caller that guessed wrong can see what it actually cleared.
  GET /v1/guardian?tenant_id= - {switches: [...killSwitches.activeFor], incidents: [...guardianIncidents.listForTenant]} so the freeze is readable over the API as well as in the banner. Because activeFor returns every scope for the tenant, this answers with the row the demo's provider-scoped trigger wrote.

NO EXISTING ROUTE CHANGES BEHAVIOUR. The page loop, /v1/events, /v1/metrics, /v1/snapshots, /v1/decisions, /v1/calibration, /v1/learnings, /v1/opportunities, /v1/experiments and both 404 envelopes are untouched, and the last /v1 handler stays last so the new routes are not shadowed.

Automation is frozen ( — ). Approve nothing until a human re-enables it.

APPROVALS SCREEN, TWO SOURCES, and which is which is stated because the previous revision read everything from one and could not have rendered a receipt. Any live write against the Meta Graph API. live.js gains no write method: the write interface is typed and the fake is the only implementation, so this slice commits to no live write contract.

Rejecting two concurrent approvals for the same action_class and resource. Nothing in this slice proposes actions, so duplicate proposals are a later slice's concern; today both execute, and test/executor/executor.test.js asserts that rather than leaving it implicit.

Account-specific maturity bands. BAND_ORDER is exported and pinned against policyBand's current output, so a re-ordering fails loudly rather than quietly inverting the floor, but which band each class should require is a calibration question this slice cannot settle from the code.
Clearing the ?meta_error simulation from the page. It is a URL-level switch with no on-page indicator, pre-existing on /, and unchanged here.

A DOM or JS-execution test harness for src/web/client.js. The three blocking defects this work order corrects I re-checked myself, at the lines the critique cited, and all three hold: routes.js:37 and :100-102 confirm the failure-injection convention has exactly one consumer today and the approve route named none; the write side defaults freeze to ('provider','meta_ads') while activeFor was specified over only the global and tenant disjuncts, so the row the demo writes was invisible to the banner, to GET /v1/guardian and to every other reader, and the envelope carries no scope for the four-key kill-switch check to read; and the reset re-stamped all four fixtures to now+24h while resetToSeed returns every one of them to status 'pending', so the lapsed fixture came back pending and step 2 of the QA script contradicted step 1 of the same script. A fourth round finding in that family is plausible and should be priced in rather than argued away, and it is why I did not simply carry the proposal's own 74 forward. validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The critique was right more often than not, and I am not going to dress that up. I re-checked every finding against the file and line it cited, and I confirmed all nine against the code rather than accepting the citations. Three blocking findings hold and all three are folded in with the mechanism named, plus five majors. The first blocker is the same defect the previous round was corrected for, recurring one route over: the proposal named the failureMode source for POST /v1/actions/execute and left the approve route saying only 'a provider built for this request', so an implementer following it literally builds that provider with the default 'ok', the write succeeds, and the failure half of AC-5 - the clause the recorded rejection was about - can never be observed. I went past the critique's suggestion and made it one providerForRequest(request) helper that the page loop and both write routes call, so the convention has a single home and a third route cannot forget it. The second blocker is new to this round and is a regression the proposal introduced: v12 defaulted freeze to scope 'global', which the two-disjunct activeFor read actually matched; v13 changed the default to ('provider','meta_ads') to exercise a real level of the four the issue names, and left activeFor over only global and tenant rows. The row the demo writes is therefore invisible to the banner, to GET /v1/guardian and to the test that asserts the freeze is readable - AC-3 unobservable end to end - and the same gap leaves the kernel's isActive port with no caller, since the envelope carries no scope. I widened the read to every scope bound to the tenant rather than narrowing the write back to global, because defaulting to 'global' would make the demo exercise the one scope whose semantics need no testing, and I named the four scope keys the check evaluates so OVER_SCOPE and KILL_SWITCH_ACTIVE have a defined path. The third blocker is a self-inflicted one: the reset re-stamped all four fixtures to now+24h while resetToSeed returns every one of them to status 'pending', so the lapsed fixture came back pending. Since step 1 IS the reset, every run failed at step 2. The fix restores the two groups differently - three pending at now+24h, the lapsed one at its original past stamp - and makes the summary print the two counts separately so '4 rows restored' is never read as '4 pending'. approved_work_order.approach:
Build the write path as six new tables behind one additive migration, four new pure-or-injected modules, one new domain module, and one composition point, then make every existing consumer of approval, posture or maturity state read through a single definition of each.

1. src/data/db.js adds migration 006 and two PRAGMAs. WAL and busy_timeout go in openDatabase, not in a route: busy_timeout is per-connection, and both the server and the seed process open through this one function, so that is the only place the setting reaches both.
2. src/data/repositories.js adds six repositories behind the same tenant-bound module contract (repositories.js:1-7): approvals (mutable working state, like experiments), capabilities (append-only), actionRecords (append-only on UPDATE, DELETE deliberately allowed - the only reason is named in db.js), killSwitches (mutable), guardianIncidents (append-only), trustLedger (mutable upsert).
3. src/domain/approvals.js is pure: validateApproval, visibleReason, isPendingApproval, partitionApprovals. One predicate decides pending versus lapsed, and four callers (the decide route, the page, the seed reset and the tests) read it instead of four implementations of it.
4. src/policy/kernel.js is the deterministic gate and the only place a write is admitted. Its roster is derived from DECISION_CLASSES by membership and its own render order is pinned, the maturity band is a FLOOR in the direction policyBand's edges already encode, the intent's action is bound to the class that registers it, capabilities are HMAC-signed, and the kill-switch check names the four scope keys it evaluates.
5. src/policy/trust.js derives one posture per class from one stored ledger row and is called by BOTH the rendered table and the gate, so the displayed posture and the enforced posture cannot disagree.
6. src/executor/executor.js is the only module that calls a provider write method, and it dedupes durably in the repository rather than in the per-request fake, which is rebuilt on every request (routes.js:103) and could not survive a second delivery.
7. src/strategy/guardian.js holds the two detectors, the named recovery predicate and the freeze, and freeze takes an explicit scope and scopeId across the four levels the issue names.
8. src/api/routes.js is the composition point and the only place maturity is computed: one helper, extracted from GET /v1/metrics, now called by the metric route and by both issuance routes, and ONE providerForRequest helper is the single source of a request's failure injection for every write route.
9. src/web/pages.js stops being a shell, and src/web/client.js grows the decide fetch, the three-way response branch and the re-decide control.
10. scripts/seed.js writes four approval fixtures, five trust rows and a --reset-approvals affordance whose nonce list is built by CALLING decisionNonce over the same seeded id list, so no prefix literal is ever written twice.

THREE RULES CARRY THE WHOLE PLAN. A PREFIX LITERAL CANNOT DRIFT IF IT IS NEVER WRITTEN: decisionNonce is the single definition and both the decide route and the reset call it. A PREDICATE CANNOT BE DISAGREED WITH IF IT IS WRITTEN ONCE: isPendingApproval has four callers and one body, the roster is one exported array with two assertions over it (set equality with DECISION_CLASSES, and its pinned order), and killSwitches.activeFor answers for every scope the same way the write side writes them. And EVERY ASSERTION A QA READER COMPARES LITERALLY HAS A NAMED MECHANISM BEHIND IT: a method, a response field, a selector or a URL - which is the defect class the last four rounds each rejected, and the rule applied to every line of qa_script below.

visibleReason(value) -> string|null. The stripped and trimmed text is what is stored, verbatim, and escapeHtml handles it on render.

  (b) A missing or unrecognised posture is a REFUSAL, never a default, and a malformed approval row is a refusal. Every ambiguous input fails closed (TR-24).
